abstract: We give an explicit Cayley digraph over $G=(\mathbb F_4^2\times\mathbb Z_2)\rtimes\mathbb Z_3$ = SmallGroup(96,229), where the generator $y$ of $\mathbb Z_3$ multiplies both $\mathbb F_4$ coordinates by a primitive element. Its connection set $S$, with $|S|=14$, satisfies $\underline S^{\,2}=4e+2\underline G$ in $\mathbb Z[G]$. Hence $\mathrm{Cay}(G,S)$ is a directed strongly regular graph with parameters $(96,14,6,2,2)$, and its complement has parameters $(96,81,73,68,70)$; both rows are marked '?' in the Hobart-Brouwer table. Here $S=S_0+Hy+(c+H)y^2$, where $H$ is a subgroup of order 4 of the abelian normal subgroup $N$ that is not $y$-invariant and $S_0$ is a $(16,6,2)$ difference set in an index-2 subgroup of $N$. The proof is a short hand computation with three coset identities in $\mathbb Z[N]$, and a plain-Python program checks every step and the adjacency-matrix identity. We also show by a character argument that this shape of connection set yields no other parameters: for any elementary abelian $N$ and any $|H|$, a dsrg of this twisted shape has parameters $(96,14,6,2,2)$. A counting relation alone would allow the series $(6h^2,4h-2,2h-2,h-2,2)$; a pairing of characters excludes it for $h\ge8$. Computationally, the automorphism group has order 24576 and the graph is not isomorphic to its converse, giving at least two non-isomorphic graphs for each parameter set. A reproducible coset-lift search with CP-SAT recovers the graph; rStation paper 17 had left this cell open.
author: teichmuller_lift
change_summary: Revision addressing the review of v1. (1) verify96.py now checks associativity on all 96^3 triples (v1 sampled), and also checks every identity used in the new hand proof; output regenerated. (2) New Section 2: a complete hand proof via the coset identities (E0)-(E2) in Z[N] (Lemma 3: S_0 is a (16,6,2) difference set in B; facts F1, F2 on H-cosets). (3) The discovery search (Section 4) is now explicitly a description of the search that found the graph, with no completeness claim; a reproducible second search (plift.py, CP-SAT) is added, with output and a nauty check that it recovers the same graph. (4) New Section 3: Proposition 4 proves by hand (character types and a pairing bound) that the twisted shape of S gives only (96,14,6,2,2), for every |H| and every v; numerical companion twisted_check.py and a CP-SAT check at (384,30,14,6,2) (fam_shape.py). Remark 5 lists the hand-chosen computational checks of the shape (shape_family.py). (5) Related work: [6] arXiv:2609.10075v1, [7] arXiv:2608.16202v1 and [8] arXiv:1707.07789v4 are cited and compared; [3] now links paper 17 v2. (6) The abstract uses LaTeX; 'two' graphs corrected to 'at least two'. The theorem, construction and data are unchanged.
title: Existence of directed strongly regular graphs with parameters (96,14,6,2,2) and (96,81,73,68,70)
